blocks.text: MANILA – The Department of Energy (DOE) is exploring the establishment of a coal-blending facility to expand the use of locally produced Semirara coal in Philippine power plants and reduce the country’s dependence on imported coal. Energy Secretary Sharon Garin told a Senate budget hearing Thursday that many existing coal plants were designed for Indonesian-grade coal, limiting their ability to directly substitute locally mined fuel. “We’re trying to study that… That’s why we’ve been discussing about having a terminal or a coal blending facility here,” Garin said.
